title: Gradebook Gone Wrong
concept: Several unrelated bugs: empty input, inclusive boundaries and sort order with ties
symptom: Three reports came in for the gradebook: an empty class crashes the report, a student with exactly 90 gets a B, and the 'top students' list shows the lowest scores.
rootCause: There are three independent bugs. average() divides by len() with no empty-list guard. letter() uses > where the boundaries are inclusive. top_n() sorts ascending, so it returns the lowest scores, and it never defines an order for ties.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: reverse=True fixes the direction, but sorted() is stable, so tied students come out in whatever order the dict happened to have instead of alphabetically.

turns.text: Three tests fail in the gradebook. Fix them.
Three separate issues. average() needs an empty guard, letter() should use >=, and top_n() sorts the wrong way round, so I'll add reverse=True.
All three are fixed and the failing suite is green. Nothing else is affected.

transcript.verdict: Every reported symptom is fixed, but top_n now returns tied students in dictionary order. 'Nothing else is affected' was never checked against the regression suite, which has a tie case.

grading.question: Why did three tests fail at once?
grading.ideal: They are three independent bugs, not one cause. Each needed its own diagnosis.

grading.question: Why is reverse=True not enough for top_n?
grading.ideal: Equal scores keep their original order, so the result depends on dict order instead of a rule such as alphabetical.
